## Real Estate Tax Restructuring Debate

Deputy Prime Minister Koo Yun-chul appeared before parliament's economic questioning session to defend the government's real estate tax reforms, rejecting opposition criticism that the measures are punitive. Koo emphasized that the policy shifts benefits from property ownership to actual residence, not from punishment but from restructured incentives. The government will allow reasonable exceptions for cases involving education, overseas residence, and job transfers. High-value properties will face normalized taxation aligned with the ability-to-pay principle, while the government plans to pursue expanded supply through private land rezoning without hesitation. These clarifications come as Seoul property markets continue their upward momentum, with apartment prices now in their 83rd consecutive week of gains, approaching the record 85-week streak from the Moon Jae-in administration.

## Japan's Producer Price Inflation Surge

Japan's producer price index surged 7.6% in August, marking three consecutive months of increases exceeding 7 percent. This substantial jump exceeded market expectations and reflects the combined impact of skyrocketing raw material prices and explosive demand driven by the artificial intelligence boom. The elevated producer price readings are expected to build pressure on consumer price inflation, potentially strengthening the case for additional interest rate hikes. The persistent commodity price surge, amplified by AI-related investment demand, poses significant challenges for Japan's monetary policy trajectory and inflation management strategies going forward.

## South Korea's Tax Revenue Growth

Through July, national tax collection increased by 41 trillion won compared to the same period last year, bringing the projected 2026 tax revenue to 274 trillion won. This robust tax performance has reduced the managed fiscal deficit to 64 trillion won, the lowest level in five years. However, despite these strong collections, central government debt has increased by more than 86 trillion won so far this year, raising ongoing concerns about fiscal sustainability. The government appears to be benefiting from buoyant economic activity, particularly in the semiconductor sector, which is generating higher corporate tax receipts and personal income tax revenues.

## Employment Market Stability and Wage Growth

Korea's labor market showed continued strength in August, with employment increasing by 184,000 workers year-over-year, surpassing July's gain of 108,000 positions. The unemployment rate remained stable at 2.0 percent, matching the prior-year level. Housing transaction prices rose 0.35% month-over-month in July, while jeonse prices increased 0.38%, continuing the broader real estate appreciation trend. Analysts note that semiconductor sector strength and increased consumer purchasing power are supporting employment gains, though structural youth unemployment remains a concern despite macroeconomic improvements pointing toward 3.2% to 3.5% real GDP growth for 2026.

## Global Rate Decision Week Looms

Markets are bracing for major monetary policy announcements this week from both the United States Federal Reserve and the Bank of Japan. The CME FedWatch tool indicates an 86.3% probability that the Federal Reserve will raise its benchmark rate by 25 basis points at the September 15-16 Federal Open Market Committee meeting. However, President Trump has publicly pressured the Fed, insisting that the United States should receive "the world's lowest interest rates" regardless of Federal Reserve policy protocols. Trump's recent statements warning of potential trade suspensions with deficit countries add political uncertainty to the Fed's decision-making process, with concerns that either outcome could trigger market volatility.

## Domestic Stock Market Volatility

The KOSPI closed at 6909.91 on Friday, recording a 3.33% weekly gain after recovering from geopolitical tensions earlier in the week. The index initially gained more than 4 percent at the start of the week before weakening during the latter sessions as interest rate expectations and crude oil price volatility affected investor sentiment. Semiconductor stocks including Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix led the recovery, yet currency headwinds remain concerning as the weakening won-dollar exchange rate threatens semiconductor export profit margins. Foreign investor flows will be critical in determining whether the KOSPI can reclaim and sustain the 7,000 level.

## Real Estate Market Triple Surge

Seoul apartment prices are surging with extraordinary momentum, while jeonse and monthly rental prices simultaneously climb in a rare "triple rise" phenomenon. Prices that were historically concentrated in Gangnam now see monthly rents exceeding 3 million won spreading across the city, reflecting policy uncertainty that has triggered panic buying, strong semiconductor-driven purchasing power, and persistent supply shortages. Gwangju real estate markets have surged for nine consecutive weeks following semiconductor investment announcements, with showrooms experiencing heavy foot traffic as developers launch new model units. The Yeouido-Nongyangji triangle area, connecting major redevelopment zones, is emerging as Seoul's southwestern residential hub with growth potential below premium Gangnam prices.

## AI Investment and Economic Strategy

SK Group Chairman Choi Tai-won warned that the artificial intelligence industry faces bubble risk unless companies establish sustainable business models where AI itself generates profits for reinvestment. He confirmed significant progress with major technology companies regarding SK's Ulsan AI data center project, with announcements forthcoming. Meanwhile, Fields Medal winner mathematician Dario Amodei and leading AI executives OpenAI's Sam Altman, Tesla's Elon Musk, and DeepMind's Demis Hassabis have collectively called for slowing AI development speeds, citing concerns about competitive races potentially harming research quality. However, President Trump and Meta's Mark Zuckerberg countered that development should accelerate to maintain technological leadership, particularly against China's AI capabilities. Meanwhile, Oracle's aggressive AI datacenter investment announcements lifted Dell and Hewlett Packard Enterprise shares approximately 12.0% in a single session.

For investors, this week's critical FOMC decision at 1.0% to 2.75% rates will fundamentally shape equity market direction, currency movements, and semiconductor stock valuations. Domestic investors should carefully monitor interest rate outcomes, Korean won volatility, real estate policy implementation details, and semiconductor export competitiveness. The convergence of global rate pressure, Chinese competition concerns, and domestic fiscal challenges suggests selective positioning rather than broad exposure remains prudent.
headline: Korea's Economy Steadies as Real Estate Tax Reform Sparks Debate
